title: Count Every Queen Arrangement (DFS + Backtracking)
real_world_story: A puzzle designer wants to know how many solutions an N-Queens board puzzle has. Queens must be placed so no two share a row, column, or diagonal, and every distinct arrangement must be counted.

real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Placing one queen per row with DFS and undoing placements that attack another queen

problem_statement: Given an integer N, count all distinct ways to place N queens on an N x N chessboard so no two queens attack each other (no shared row, column, or diagonal).
task: Return the number of distinct valid arrangements.
input_format: A single line containing integer N.
output_format: Print the number of distinct valid queen arrangements.

examples.explanation: A 4x4 board has exactly 2 safe arrangements.

expected_algorithm.name: Backtracking
expected_algorithm.reason: One queen is placed per row with column and diagonal pruning, and each placement is undone to explore the next option.

hint: Place queens row by row so rows never clash.
Track used columns, main diagonals, and anti-diagonals.
Remove the queen after recursing to the next row.
real_world_takeaway: DFS with pruning counts every valid combinatorial puzzle layout without enumerating hopeless branches.
